cards.b: Metals: good thermal and electrical conductors, malleable, ductile, high melting points. Non-metals: poor conductors, brittle (solids).
Potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium, aluminium, carbon, zinc, iron, hydrogen, copper, silver, gold.
K, Na, Ca react (hydroxide + hydrogen). Mg reacts with steam to give oxide + hydrogen.
Reactive metals give salt + hydrogen. Copper, silver and gold do not react.
A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its salt solution.
A mixture of a metal with other elements. Brass: copper + zinc. Stainless steel: iron + chromium, nickel, carbon.

cards.f: Why are alloys harder than pure metals?
cards.b: Different sized atoms stop the layers sliding over each other easily.
Both oxygen and water must be present.
Paint, grease/oil, plastic coating: exclude oxygen and water.
A more reactive metal (e.g. zinc) corrodes instead of iron because it loses electrons more easily.
Coating iron/steel with zinc: barrier plus sacrificial protection.
Metals below carbon are reduced with carbon; metals above carbon need electrolysis.
Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. Limestone forms slag (CaSiO₃) with impurities.
About 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen; rest noble gases and carbon dioxide.

short.q: Explain why alloys are harder than pure metals. [2]
short.model: The atoms in an alloy are different sizes, so the layers cannot slide over each other easily.

short.q: Write the equation for the reduction of iron(III) oxide in the blast furnace and state the role of limestone. [3]
short.model: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂; limestone removes impurities by forming slag.

short.q: Explain how galvanising protects steel even when the zinc coating is scratched. [3]
short.model: Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it loses electrons in preference and corrodes instead of iron (sacrificial protection).

short.q: State the source and one adverse effect of sulfur dioxide and carbon monoxide. [4]
short.model: SO₂: burning fossil fuels containing sulfur; acid rain. CO: incomplete combustion of carbon-containing fuels; toxic.

short.q: Describe how water is treated to make it safe for the domestic supply. [3]
short.model: Sedimentation and filtration remove solids; carbon removes tastes and odours; chlorine kills microbes.
